# E7 — the gate as a classifier: every saved candidate judged again by the harness, each check on its own, DataRaceBench as the outside ground truth for races

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done 12 Nov — Part A (both corpora) and Part B read out (thesis, section 'How often the gate is wrong')

## The question

How often did the gate accept a wrong change or refuse a right one, what did each check decide alone, and how much rests on the second input? (RQ2, C2, H3) — on the 3,034 candidates saved in E1-v6 and E2-v6b, the 248 directives of the six no-model draws of DiscoPoP alone, and DataRaceBench's labelled kernels. No model call.

## Result in one paragraph

No model call. Part A, every saved candidate judged again by the harness (per distinct program): the model's rewrites inside the agent (E1-v6 and E2-v6b) — 10 of 357 right ones refused (2.8 %), all reordered floating-point sums, and 19 of 310 wrong ones accepted (6.1 %), all crashing only at the verification size (18 stack arrays of the loop's length, 1 allocation per repetition), none a trial's final file; DiscoPoP's directives inside the agent — 1 of 422 right ones refused (read by hand: a real loop-carried dependence the judge does not show) and 0 of 47 wrong ones accepted; DiscoPoP's own directives (six no-model draws) — 7 of 115 right ones refused (6 by time limits on a three-iteration loop of md, 1 by the dependence-stage defect Fix 105 repaired) and 0 of 71 wrong ones accepted. Each check alone: no unique catch for any check on the agent's corpus; on DiscoPoP's own directives the sanitizer is the only check to refuse 8 of 71, the schedule matrix none, each single input none (the perturbed input is the only output comparison to refuse 22, which the sanitizer refuses too). H3 refuted on both registered criteria. Of the races the gate's sanitizer reports in every run at the small size, the judge's race check at the verification size reports 2 of 13 on the agent's corpus and 57 of 63 on DiscoPoP's own directives. Part B, DataRaceBench 1.4.1: one call of the gate refuses 66 of 79 documented races and 7 of 67 race-free kernels (all seven print thread-dependent output).

| 2026-11-12 | result | **E7 Part A read out, complete on both corpora — the gate against the harness (A1: `e7_a1_judge_1`, `e7_a1_judge_2`, `e7_a1_judge_3`, `e7_a1_judge_4`, `e7_a1_judge_5`, `e7_a1_checks`, `e7_a1_checks_2`; A2: `e7_a2_judge_1`, `e7_a2_judge_2`, `e7_a2_checks`; server, no model; archived, valid; `gate_study.py readout` without `--partial` → `analysis/readout_a1.md`, `readout_a2.md` and their `.json`; every disagreement read by hand, `analysis/by_hand/README.md`). The gate accepted no wrong directive on either corpus and no rewrite that computes a wrong value; the 19 wrong rewrites it accepted crash at a size it does not run, and none was shipped. It refused 10 of 357 right rewrites, all reordered floating-point sums. H3 is refuted on both of its registered criteria.** *Coverage.* A1: 3,034 candidates on 1,395 distinct programs in 42 benchmarks, every program judged, all 1,449 (base, program) pairs replayed; A2: 248 candidates, 187 programs, 39 benchmarks, 187 pairs, likewise complete. The replayed whole gate gives the recorded verdict again on 1,448 of 1,449 and 186 of 187 pairs; the two differences are stages the replay does not hold (the clause check on `tsvc_c3/s331` #75, the dependence stage on `polybench/mvt` #3). The harness finds every program that was a trial's final file right again (121 of 121, 65 of 65). *R1, per distinct program (per candidate and per loop in the read-outs; Wilson 95 %).* **A1, the model's rewrites:** right 357, of which the gate refused 10 (2.8 %, 1.5–5.1 %); wrong 310, of which it accepted 19 (6.1 %, 4.0–9.4 %); 217 texts refused before a program exists, and the judge's build fails for all 217. **A1, DiscoPoP's directives inside the agent:** right 422, refused 1 (0.2 %, 0.0–1.3 %); wrong 47, accepted 0 (one-sided 95 % bound 6.2 %); 41 programs sit on one of the 19 accepted rewrites that crash and are counted apart, as registered for a base that fails (29 accepted, 12 refused); one does not build. **A2, DiscoPoP's own directives:** right 115, refused 7 (6.1 %, 3.0–12.0 %); wrong 71, accepted 0 (bound 4.1 %); one does not build. *What the disagreements are (read one by one).* (a) **The 19 accepted wrong rewrites** give the original's values exactly on both inputs at the small size and end with a segmentation fault at the verification size: 18 hold an array of the loop's length on the stack, 1 allocates a copy per repetition (tested: three of the 18 run to the end with the stack limit raised). None is a trial's final file; each was reverted in the next step — 12 by the crash of the timed run at the timing size, 5 because DiscoPoP's only directive failed the gate, 1 as not faster, 1 as holding no pattern. (b) **The 10 refused right rewrites** reorder floating-point operations (`s3112` 5, `s323` 4, `s322` 1) and differ from the original by 7·10⁻¹⁶ to 4·10⁻¹¹ relative, under the harness's 10⁻⁹; the gate compares these benchmarks byte for byte because their measured noise is zero. (c) **A1's one refused right directive is not right** (`s341` #16, a parallel loop on a running sum): the gate's sanitizer reports it in every run, the judge's instruments do not show it. (d) **A2's seven refused right directives:** six `burkardt/md` programs refused by time limits (the row below, (1)), and `mvt` #3 refused by the dependence stage through the line-number defect that Fix 105 repaired on 9 Oct, the day after that trial. (e) **Three of A2's 71 wrong programs are correct up to the order of two sums** (`md` #8 #10 #11, `reduction(+:pe,ke)`): tested, only the printed relative energy error, a difference of nearly equal numbers, exceeds the tolerance; both the gate and the judge refuse them, and they stay counted as wrong. *R2, each check alone on the wrong pairs (at least one of three runs; no refusal of a wrong pair is a time limit).* **A1 directives, 47:** the whole gate 47, the sanitizer 12, the schedule matrix 46, the output on the shipped input 47, on the perturbed input 47; no check is the only one to refuse any. **A2 directives, 71:** the whole gate 71, the sanitizer 63, the matrix 38, the shipped input 41, the perturbed input 61; the sanitizer is the only check to refuse 8, no other check any. **A1 rewrites, 310:** each input alone refuses the same 291; 19 are refused by neither (a). Right pairs refused by a check alone: A1 rewrites 6 on the shipped and 9 on the perturbed input (b); A1 directives 1 by the sanitizer (c); A2 the six `md` programs by every check's time limit. The matrix's soft verdict stands on 38 and 8 wrong pairs and on no right one. *By kind of check (added, see the row below, (4)):* A2 — the sanitizer, the matrix and the output 33; the sanitizer and the output 22; the sanitizer only 8; the matrix and the output 5; the output only 3. A1 — the matrix and the output 34; all three 12; the output only 1. The sanitizer's 8 are real races that leave the printed values right (a shared inner-loop counter in `doitgen` and `reg_detect`, reads of matrix elements another thread writes in `floyd-warshall`); the output's 3 are `md` with `nd` private and read uninitialised; `pathfinder`'s parallel `rand()` loop is refused by the matrix and the output and passes the sanitizer. *R3, the second input.* A1: no wrong pair, rewrite or directive, is refused by the output on the perturbed input only. A2: 22 of the 71 wrong pairs pass the output comparison on the shipped input in every run and fail it on the perturbed input in every run (`dynprog` 6, `ludcmp` 4, `trisolv` 4, `gramschmidt` 3, `seidel-2d` 3, `jacobi-2d-imper` 1, `lu` 1 — PolyBench kernels whose shipped input is a regular function of the indices); the sanitizer refuses all 22; 2 pairs (`pathfinder`) fail on the shipped input only. *The judge's limits, measured.* Its race check at the verification size reports a race on 2 of the 13 A1 pairs and 57 of the 63 A2 pairs on which the gate's sanitizer, alone, reports one in every run at the small size; in 16 of the 17 silent cases the judge's value comparison finds the program wrong anyway. Tested on three of them: the report appears at the small size in 12 of 12 runs and at the verification size in 1 of 26, whichever optimisation level, also with the sanitizer's largest history; the cause is not established. "No wrong directive accepted" therefore means none the judge could see; Part B's figure (one call of the gate refuses 66 of 79 documented races) is the measure against an outside ground truth. *Against the registration.* **H3 is refuted on both criteria:** the judge finds false accepts (19 rewrites in A1), and checks have no unique catch — the schedule matrix and each single input on both corpora, the sanitizer on A1. The sanitizer has unique catches on A2 only. *Expectations:* held — no false accept among final files, the false accepts among candidates the agent undid and of the kind named (data-sized arrays on the stack), the false refusals of rewrites all reordered floating-point sums, few unique catches for the matrix (none); not held — a unique catch for the perturbed input (none; it is the only OUTPUT comparison to refuse 22 wrong programs of A2, which the sanitizer refuses too). As registered, a check without a unique catch stays in the agent and is reported as redundant on this corpus: the schedule matrix on both. *What decides what.* No result of E1-v6 or E2-v6b changes. The thesis gets the gate's measured error as a section of its own after §6.2, and the sentences that rested on the early study of the second input are rewritten per kind of candidate; with Part B (the row of 11 Nov) group E7 is done | Result, E7 Part A |

| 2026-11-12 | deviation | **E7: the corpus builder had put the candidates of 10 trials of A1 on the wrong file. Found reading the large corpus's false accepts by hand; repaired before any number of A1 is read; 14 programs and 15 pairs are judged in an added run, registered here before it starts (`e7_a1_judge_5`, `e7_a1_checks_2`; no model).** *What ran first.* The main runs of A1 ended without a tool error (`e7_a1_judge_1`, `e7_a1_judge_2`, `e7_a1_judge_3`, `e7_a1_judge_4`, `e7_a1_checks`; server, four 12-core groups, 11 Nov 20:42 – 12 Nov 11:20 UTC at `6224a5c8c`; 1,389 programs judged, 1,443 pairs replayed; fetched and archived). *What was found.* The first read-out named 21 accepted programs the judge finds wrong. Two were DiscoPoP's directive on the repetition loop of `tsvc_c2/s331`, with `dummy` inside the loop — a text today's replay refuses in every run by every check. The trial's own log shows the directive judged on another text: an earlier rewrite, kept at that time, had moved `dummy` out of the loop. *The cause, mine.* `gate_study.py corpus` took "this rewrite was kept" from `accepted.json`, which is the state after the agent's last steps. In 10 of the 431 trials a last step undoes something after the last candidate was judged: Settle dropped a rewrite (6 trials), the floor shipped DiscoPoP's own program (3), a directive that passed was deferred as slower alone (2, one of them among the 6). There, 13 candidates judged after such a rewrite were put on the file without it (6 of them only because the builder let a patch apply inexactly), and 11 accepted directives of the final pass could not be rebuilt at all — the "11 not rebuilt" of the registration. The corpus had listed these 10 trials as `not_verified` since its first build; the registration row did not mention the list and I had not read it as the warning it was. *The repair* (`0d2fc8966`). The builder follows each trial's own log: a rewrite is kept when the log says `ACCEPTED` without a revert, a final-pass directive is applied when it says `APPLIED`, and every patch has to apply exactly. Checked on all 431 trials: log lines and candidate records line up one for one (562 rewrites that passed the gate = 293 kept + 269 reverted; 534 final-pass directives that passed = 532 applied + 2 deferred); the 421 trials outside the ten give the same candidates as before; all 3,034 candidates are rebuilt, none inexactly; 422 trials end in the archived final file byte for byte and 9 end before a named last step (`ended_later`). A2 rebuilt with the repaired builder is identical in programs, candidates and files (no rewrite, no last step there), so its runs are not touched. *What changes in A1.* Candidates 3,023 → 3,034; distinct programs judged 1,389 → 1,395 (with a directive 506 → 511; accepted 816, refused 579); pairs 1,443 → 1,449. Eight programs leave the corpus, texts the gate never saw (seven of `tsvc_c2/s331`, one of `tsvc_c2/vpvtv`); 13 enter, all of `tsvc_c2/s331`; one more (`tsvc_c2/s244` #10, a trial's final file) is now a candidate's program. Programs keep their numbers, new ones get numbers above them (`--previous`), so every record of the main runs still names its program; the first build stays in the repository as `corpus/a1/corpus_2026-11-11.json`. *The added run.* `analysis/e7_added.sh`, one 12-core group, after the A2 runs end and the server is synced: the same judge and checks commands, restricted by `--added-since` to the 14 programs and 15 pairs the first build lacks (`e7_a1_judge_5`, `e7_a1_checks_2`).
